postpartum), as well as infants and children (up to age 5; see 
Chapter 9). For women, “nutritional risk” criteria may include 
anemia, poor gestational weight gain, and inadequate diet, 
as well as a variety of preexisting medical conditions. WIC 
provides targeted supplemental foods, nutrition education and 
breastfeeding support, as well as health care referrals. Outcome 
studies show improved birth weights and higher mean gesta-
tional ages in infants born to WIC participants.
Many pregnant women have limited knowledge regarding the 
nutrients in the supplements they have been advised to purchase.
